pairs.subject: background-jobs
pairs.evidence: src/api/pipeline/workflows.ts:15 cancelWorkflowJob resolves void while the backend writes the terminal state at once as Failed (src-tauri/src/background_job.rs:684) and WorkflowJob omits cancel_outcome (src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/workflows.rs:18), so no client can show cancelling or tell cancelled from failed

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/background_job.rs:684 cancel() writes status failed in the same call that fires the token, so the cancelling and cancelled steps collapse into one, and JobStatus has no cancelled terminal; the WorkflowJob projection (src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/workflows.rs:18) drops cancel_outcome even though the command doc at :134 says the snapshot reports it. Identity (jobType+jobId) and the bounded 20-line snapshot tail (:75, exposed at src/api/pipeline/workflows.ts:9) are realized

src/api/pipeline/scheduler.ts:13 getSchedulerStatus returns per-loop SubscriptionHealth with alive, consecutivePanics and lastTickAt (src/lib/bindings/SubscriptionHealth.ts:35), so a loop that stops ticking shows up because it goes silent
src/api/pipeline/scheduler.ts:40 listScheduleMissedRuns exposes the offline-gap record the sweep keeps, separate from live runs; backfill is an explicit operator act
src/api/pipeline/scheduler.ts:16 one start/stop door is exposed, but the roster, stop handles and shutdown order live in the backend scheduler, which is outside this context and was not read
src/lib/bindings/SubscriptionHealth.ts:31 consecutivePanics shows a panic boundary exists; per-tick deadlines and quarantine are backend-side and were not read here
src/api/pipeline/scheduler.ts:13 these are IPC wrappers with no cadence of their own; the cadence lives in the backend scheduler and was not read here

pairs.registryProposal: Two findings. (1) Re-verified, same digest: the deviation was judged earlier today and still holds. getWorkflowsOverview and cancelWorkflowJob have ZERO callers under src/ (grep 2026-10-10), so the contract gap is latent in an IPC surface no UI uses yet. An unwired job-control surface is a case job-progress-and-cancellation could name: a cancel IPC shipped before any viewer exists hardens the collapsed contract. (2) Missing pairing: the backend runtime this subject actually governs (src-tauri/src/background_job.rs BackgroundJobManager and the scheduler subscription loops behind SubscriptionHealth) has no background-jobs pair. This api-pipeline wrapper context, at probable confidence, is the subject's only pair in the map. The techniques the wrapper cannot evidence (loop-supervision, tick-isolation, adaptive-cadence) need that backend context paired to be judged at all.
